links.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of LLM responses versus 6th-grade patient education target
links.effect: Mean FKGL of all 3 models was collegiate level or higher; all responses exceeded the AMA/NIH-recommended 6th-grade reading level. Gemini less readable than ChatGPT (P = .03).
links.quote: Regarding readability, the mean FKGL of all 3 models was at a collegiate level or higher, and all responses exceeded the American Medical Association and National Institutes of Health-recommended 6th-grade reading level for patient education.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient-directed responses relative to recommended 6th-grade level
links.effect: All responses from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok exceeded the 6th-grade reading level; mean FKGL at collegiate level or higher.
links.quote: Regarding readability, the mean FKGL of all 3 models was at a collegiate level or higher, and all responses exceeded the American Medical Association and National Institutes of Health-recommended 6th-grade reading level for patient education.

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of LLM responses to orthobiologic questions (CRRS, AIRM)
links.effect: Accuracy generally acceptable, but 50% (10/20) of ChatGPT, 25% (5/20) of Gemini, and 30% (6/20) of Grok responses needed more than minimal clarification (CRRS >2); Gemini more accurate than ChatGPT (CRRS P = .04).
links.quote: While response accuracy was generally acceptable, 50% (10/20) of ChatGPT, 25% (5/20) of Gemini, and 30% (6/20) of Grok responses were deemed as requiring more than minimal clarification (CRRS >2).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the accuracy and readability of three commercial LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok) answering patient questions about orthobiologic injections using expert clinician ratings and readability formulas, but does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
